judge.notes: Only rank 1 (Firestore schema drift) genuinely voices the duplicate-schema/drift pain, and it is locked; rank 2 is a tangential 'validate AI-generated files' pipeline, and rank 3 is a 2022 StackOverflow question about compile-time generic indexing that the pipeline itself rescored at 0.05 confidence — three-for-three rejected means zero actionable intent surfaced. Replies do lead with a diagnosis and carry a clear 'I built it' disclosure with a takeaway that stands without the link, but all three share one rigid template ('Disclosure: I built it. Even if you skip it...'), never quote thread specifics, omit the alpha/0.4.x instability the ICP would want to know, and #3 is shoehorned onto a question about lens typing where a link-drop would be flagged on SO. Queries include three strong ICP-voice reddit searches ('tired of writing zod schema for every typescript interface', 'runtime validation without duplicating types') but the rest are terse keyword fragments, and 'typescript schema sync agent coordination' is off-domain noise; no queries mine the buying trigger (prod incident from API response drift) or competitor names beyond Zod (typia, io-ts, valibot).

All four signals were rescored as rejected with 0.92-0.97 confidence, and the rejections are correct: an ops-triage-agent PRD, a SharePoint hackathon submission, a memory-plugin slot architecture RFC, and an open-source policy debate about AI contributions. None contains a head of support (or anyone) complaining that their bot deflects nothing or invents answers — the 'why_relevant' notes even concede 'low signal' twice while still ranking them. The replies are individually literate and do engage with thread specifics before disclosing builder status, but every one ends with the same bolt-on pivot ('different domain but same retrieval-confidence pattern'), which in a gbdev policy RFC or a hackathon submission reads as pure drive-by promotion a moderator would remove. Queries lean heavily on GitHub/StackOverflow issue search where support leads never post, repeat near-identical hallucination phrasings, and never mine competitor-switching language (Fin/Chatbase complaints), deflection-rate targets, or support-community venues.

The single signal is a self-authored project task issue ("Step 17: Add staging monitoring...") on someone's own repo backlog — a todo item, not a person expressing the pain of click-ops monitors or an unnoticed outage. The pipeline itself labels intent_strength "low" yet the rescore upgrades it to "relevant" at 0.72, an unjustified inflation. The drafted reply is technically literate and discloses authorship, but it asserts specifics ("your acceptance criteria call for Terraform-defined uptime checks", Cloud Run URLs, Cloud Tasks resources) not evidenced by the quoted title, and dropping a vendor pitch into a stranger's internal task tracker is exactly what maintainers flag as spam. Queries are the strongest part: they mix subreddit targeting, HN Algolia, GitHub and SO, and use real ICP phrasings ("alternative to UptimeRobot", "Datadog too expensive", "dead man snitch"), though they miss the profile's own trigger language like "outage nobody noticed" or "monitors as code" on non-Reddit surfaces.
